candidate.blueprint_topic: Medication procedure teaching and local adverse-effect prevention
candidate.educational_objective: Explain that intra-articular corticosteroid injections may provide short-term osteoarthritis symptom relief but repeated frequent injections into the same joint can cause local harm, so frequency should be individualized rather than treated as unlimited.

options.A: These injections can provide short-term symptom relief, but repeated frequent injections into the same joint may cause local tissue or joint damage, so timing is individualized rather than scheduled without limit.
options.B: Corticosteroid injections have no meaningful effect on osteoarthritis pain, so repeating them serves no therapeutic purpose in any client.
options.C: The injections must be given every day to maintain an anti-inflammatory effect, and missed daily injections cause rebound arthritis.
options.D: Repeated injections into the same joint are known to be risk-free, so there is no clinical reason to consider cumulative local effects.

candidate.rationale: A is correct. AAOS patient and clinical resources state that intra-articular corticosteroid injections can provide short-term relief of osteoarthritis pain and swelling, while repeated frequent injections into the same joint may cause damage or other negative local effects. Therefore, clinicians do not treat injection frequency as unlimited or automatic. B is incorrect because AAOS recognizes a role for short-term pain relief. C invents a daily dosing model that is not used for intra-articular corticosteroid treatment. D contradicts the recognized concern about repeated local exposure. The final item deliberately avoids a universal maximum number of injections per year because practice decisions are individualized and the tested construct is the reason repeated frequent injections are limited, not memorization of a numeric rule.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Current AAOS resources directly support short-term symptomatic benefit from intra-articular corticosteroid injections and concern for damage/negative local effects with repeated frequent injections into the same joint, without establishing a universal frequency rule for every client.
